contracts.commit_point: The tool-dispatch interception point: `forbidden_dml_check` returns the blocking dict at agent.py:86 before the `execute_sql` tool executes; a `None` return at agent.py:89 (or a non-matching query) allows the `execute_sql` call to proceed to BigQuery execution.
contracts.declared_mechanism: `forbidden_dml_check` (agent.py:74-89): logs the tool call args, and when `tool.name == 'execute_sql'` extracts `args.get('query')`, normalizes it (upper/strip), and returns a blocking result dict `{"result": "Tool execution was blocked by before_tool_callback due to a DML statement."}` if any forbidden keyword word-matches; registered as `before_tool_callback=forbidden_dml_check` on `bq_investigation_agent` (agent.py:156) and `decision_agent` (agent.py:222).
contracts.forbidden_condition: Execution of a BigQuery SQL query — the `query` argument of an `execute_sql` tool call — whose uppercased, stripped text contains any word-boundary occurrence of the forbidden DML keywords UPDATE, DELETE, MERGE, or TRUNCATE (agent.py:83-86), i.e., destructive DML reaching BigQuery execution.

contracts.protected_operation: Invocation of the `execute_sql` tool (supplied by `bigquery_toolset`/`BigQueryToolset`) with the agent-supplied `query` argument, which would execute that SQL against the BigQuery project/dataset on behalf of the SOC investigation and decision agents.

contracts.protection_obligation: Before any BigQuery `execute_sql` tool call executes on the BigQuery-capable agents (`bq_investigation_agent` and `decision_agent`), a SQL query containing any forbidden DML keyword (UPDATE, DELETE, MERGE, TRUNCATE) must be blocked, enforced by the `forbidden_dml_check` callback registered as `before_tool_callback` on both agents. (Merges the phase-one and phase-two reviewer wordings, which describe the same obligation.)
scope_limits: Only the four keywords UPDATE, DELETE, MERGE, TRUNCATE are forbidden (agent.py:83); other destructive operations (e.g., DROP, INSERT, CREATE OR REPLACE, DDL, stored procedure calls) are not blocked by this mechanism.

The regex matches keywords anywhere in the query text with word boundaries after uppercasing/stripping (agent.py:84-85); it does not parse statement position or SQL semantics, so it may over-block benign SELECT queries containing these words and offers no protection against obfuscation.

The check applies only to tools whose name is exactly 'execute_sql' (agent.py:79); other tools in the agents' tool lists (e.g., get_visual_analysis_for_user, generate_signed_url, log_false_positive) pass through the callback unblocked.

Registration is per-agent: only `bq_investigation_agent` and `decision_agent` declare `before_tool_callback=forbidden_dml_check`; the orchestrator agents (`investigation_agent`, `root_agent`, agent.py:229-242) do not register it, so coverage of any invocation path not dispatched through these two agents is not established by the supplied source.

The prompt-level rule 'NEVER, EVER DELETE OR MODIFY ANY EXISTING DATA IN BIGQUERY' (agent.py:152) is instruction text only and is not an enforcement mechanism; the callback is the sole declared guard.
